capabilities: Track reading time per document with focused/away/idle/paused channels
Show daily and weekly totals plus a four-track heatmap in a sidebar view
Run an independent stopwatch with pause, resume and notes
Run countdown, pomodoro and irregular-interval plans
Edit recorded sessions and classify each segment as reading, paused or ignored
disambiguation: Not a task or project timer; it measures reading time per document and keeps two independent manual timers.
extras: Refactor release (v1.8.2): storage moved from JSON to SQLite (sql.js/WASM) and source split into TypeScript modules under src/. No history migration: the new database starts empty and the old JSON file is left untouched. Requires Obsidian 1.15.0 or newer because the countdown flow diagram uses the built-in Pele renderer via loadMermaid(). Installation is manual: copy manifest.json plus four runtime files from dist/ (including sql-wasm.wasm) into the plugin folder. Known sync limitation: concurrent writes from multiple devices can resurrect deleted records, and deletion sync is not implemented. Mobile foreground/background detection relies on Capacitor appStateChange and pause/resume events plus Page Lifecycle, with heartbeat-gap fallback when the process is killed.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to see how much time is spent reading each document, nor any standalone stopwatch or countdown timer.
summary: Sidebar plugin that tracks reading time per document (focused vs. away), plus separate stopwatch and countdown timers, with data in SQLite.
